local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 South Dakota's counties elect commissioners from odd-numbered and at-large districts, auditors, sheriffs and registers of deeds, and voters also choose conservation district supervisors, water development district directors from odd-numbered areas and three Heartland Consumers Power District directors. Each city and each school board picks the June primary date or the November date for its own election: this year the Secretary of State's June 2 list named 140 municipal and 88 school board candidates, and its November list names 39 city and town candidates in ten places and no school board candidate. Townships choose their officers at the annual meeting on the first Tuesday of March, and county treasurers, state's attorneys and coroners are regularly elected in presidential years.
local_calendar.s: SDCL 7-7-1.1, 7-8-1, 8-3-1, 8-3-2, 9-13-1, 13-7-10 and 38-8-39; South Dakota Secretary of State, Offices to be Filled in 2026, and its 2026 primary and general election candidate lists

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Candidate List: 357 county contests in all 66 counties, 14 city and town contests in ten places, 38 conservation district contests, 21 water development district director areas (9 more are up with no candidate on the list) and 3 Heartland Consumers Power District subdivisions, with 562 candidates; 2 who withdrew are left off. The list does not say how many are elected in a contest or which contests fill an unexpired term, and candidates for county office file with the county auditor, so an office missing from the list is no proof that no one is running; a candidate with no opponent is elected without being printed on the ballot (SDCL 12-16-1.1), and write-in votes are not counted (SDCL 12-20-21.2). Not loaded: ballot questions, local primaries, school boards, and any city or town that votes in November without being on the state list.

measures.t: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution that Repeals Expanded Medicaid Coverage if Federal Funding for the Program Drops below 90%.
measures.s:
Medicaid is a program, funded by the State and the federal government, to provide medical coverage for low-income children, pregnant women, disabled individuals, and the elderly. In the 2022 General Election the voters approved Constitutional Amendment D, which expanded Medicaid eligibility in South Dakota. Amendment D requires the State to also provide Medicaid benefits to anyone over the age of 18 and under 65 whose income is at or below 133% of the federal property level, plus 5% of the federal poverty level for the applicable family size. Currently, federal law requires the federal government to fund 90% of South Dakota’s Medicaid expansion.
This proposed Constitutional Amendment ends the expanded Medicaid coverage if the federal funding for expansion drops below 90%. If federal funding drops below that 90% threshold, Medicaid coverage will once again only apply to low-income children, pregnant women, disabled individuals, and the elderly.

measures.t: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution Clarifying that an Individual Must Be a Citizen of the United States to be Eligible to Vote.
measures.s:
Article VII, § 2 of the South Dakota Constitution defines who is qualified to vote in state elections. Among these qualifications are age, residency, and United States citizenship requirements. Article VII, § 2 also establishes that individuals may be disqualified from voting because of mental incompetence or a felony conviction.
This constitutional amendment adds people who are not United States citizens to the list of individuals disqualified from voting, clarifying the existing requirement that only citizens may vote in state elections.

measures.t: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution Establishing the Trust for Unclaimed Property Fund.
measures.s:
Under South Dakota statute, intangible property is presumed to be abandoned if it remains unclaimed by the owner for more than three years after it became payable or distributable. Examples of intangible property are traveler’s checks, money orders, bank deposits, refunds, stocks, funds owed under a life insurance policy, and property held in a safe deposit box. Abandoned intangible property is transferred to the State Treasurer to hold while waiting for the owner to claim it. The State Treasurer must provide public notice of the abandoned property.
This proposed constitutional amendment establishes a trust fund where unclaimed abandoned property will be deposited. Portions of the interest and income from this fund will be distributed into the general fund for the benefit of the state. This proposed amendment requires the Legislature to determine the amount to be distributed that promotes the growth of the trust fund and the distributed amount.

methods: lists

Who is running comes only from the South Dakota Secretary of State’s own lists of candidates for the November 3 general election and the June 2 primary, and the official primary results; each file is named below, with where it was read. The U.S. Senate and House races are on the Congress pages. County and local contests are read from the lists named below too: which local offices are on this ballot, what was read and what is not here yet are set out under County by county, in the words of the notes kept with the lists.
lists

What is read from the lists. The office and the district or place it belongs to, the candidate’s name, the party, the ballot order where the list gives one, the official primary vote counts where they are loaded, and the campaign website where a candidate listed one. Addresses, phone numbers and e-mail in the lists are never read, kept or shown.
lists

Parties. Offices elected on party lines show the party each candidate filed under, written out. Among the county and local contests here, county offices are elected on party lines; conservation districts, cities, towns and other districts are nonpartisan. Each contest’s own page says which, from the list it was read from.
lists

Primaries. Where more people ran in a primary (June 2) than it could send on, everyone on that primary ballot is shown, with who went on to November, read from the general election list. Vote counts are the official results where they are loaded; where they are not, the race says so.
lists
Order. Candidates appear in the ballot order the list gives, or by surname where it gives none. Never by money, polls or party.
places

Places. A county or local contest is filed under every county it reaches. The names of cities, towns and districts come from the U.S. Census Bureau and the South Dakota Secretary of State, each named among these sources; where something on a county’s ballot could not be shown, that county’s page says what and why.
holders

Who holds a seat today (the Legislature and the statewide offices the roster carries) comes from the Open States roster the record side of this site uses. A candidate matched to a sitting legislator by district and name, one fit only, links to their record page, and their birth date, terms and portrait come from that roster before anything else.
maps

The map and “use my location”. The lines on the map of “your ballot” come from the U.S. Census Bureau, the South Dakota Department of Education, the State of South Dakota, the South Dakota Department of Agriculture and Natural Resources and the South Dakota Legislature: precincts, the districts put together from whole precincts, and the larger districts’ own lines; each source’s own notice is shown with the map. The Legislature’s page draws the Census Bureau’s cartographic boundary files. Your location is used on your own device to find your precinct and is never sent anywhere. The exact spot is not kept: what stays on the device until you tap “Forget” is your precinct with its districts and a rounded copy of the spot (about half a mile). A typed address goes from your device straight to the U.S. Census Bureau’s address finder, only when you press Look up; only the spot it finds comes back, used the same way, and this site never sees or keeps the address. Street pictures are off until you switch them on; then they come from OpenStreetMap’s servers, which see which map squares are asked for. Your county’s sample ballot is the authority on your ballot.
page
Nobody is scored or graded. The cards show the record; the judging is yours.
people

Who the candidates are. For statewide offices, the Legislature, county offices, mayors and city councils a card may show a photo, an age, the public offices a candidate has held, the government’s own page about an officeholder, the campaign’s website and the headings of its issues page. Official records come first; the rest was found on the open web by one reader and confirmed against the page that states it by a second, and a finding counts only when its source ties the person to this race. Each is labelled by its source and linked to it. Candidates for soil and water, hospital and other small district boards and city clerks and treasurers show what they filed and, if they listed one, their campaign website. Never collected, for anyone: home or mailing addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, family, marital status, religion, health, ethnicity, income, employers, schools or legal troubles. No social media profile, people-search site, data broker or voter file is ever a source, and nobody was contacted.
web

Found on the open web. A birth year or an office held is labelled by the kind of page that states it: “according to” a government’s own page or the campaign, “as reported by” Wikipedia or a named news organization. An age from a birth year alone reads “about”, and offices found this way are listed, never added up into years of service. A blank means nothing was found, not that there is nothing.
own

Campaign websites. A candidate’s website is the address they filed with the list, or the campaign’s own site found on the open web and checked against the race it names; the race’s page says which. An address that no longer leads to the campaign is left out.
own
In their own words. The topics a campaign’s issues page lists are shown as headings, with a link to the page; nothing is summarized. Photos from a campaign’s own site are credited to it and linked.
page

The record, not a label. For a nonpartisan office a race’s page shows only what is on the record: a party’s own published endorsement, an earlier run or office under a party label, and the candidate’s own words on their own campaign site, each linked to where it stands. This site never calls a person or a place by a party of its own choosing.
results

How a place has voted. For a nonpartisan office the race’s page shows how the place voted in past partisan elections: the official precinct results, added up here by county and district on the lines in force at that election; the results read here give no figures for a city, town, village or township, and the page says so there. It is not a prediction, it says nothing about any candidate or voter, and where very few people voted the split is left out.
polls

Polls of the statewide races are shown only from pollsters in the American Association for Public Opinion Research’s Transparency Initiative, who publish how each poll was done: the latest from up to five of them, each checked against the pollster’s own release, and our own average of the ten most recent, with the arithmetic shown. Polls by other pollsters are counted and named, not shown. A poll is a measure of opinion when it was taken, with a margin of error, not a forecast.
polls

Betting markets. Prices on Polymarket, a prediction market, are shown for the statewide races it lists, as information only: not a poll, not a forecast and not an official record. They are read from its public data, and prices move all day. Where Kalshi or PredictIt (two other markets) lists a race, the page says so and links to it, but shows none of its prices: their terms do not allow other sites to show them. A notice comes before any link to a market. The Civic Archive takes no money from any market and uses no referral links.
lists

The contests for Congress at the top of your ballot are the Congress pages’ own, from the state’s official candidate list: each name as printed, with its party label, in the ballot order the list gives (or by surname where it gives none), with its write-in and incumbent marks. Everything else about those candidates is on their race’s Congress page. Your U.S. House district is found without asking: the whole state is one district.
rules

Ballot questions. Each question’s official texts are shown word for word: the question as it will be printed and, where the record has them, the official summary, what a yes and a no vote do and the fiscal note, each labelled by who wrote it where the record says, and by its source. Where this site puts something in its own words (often the votes needed to pass and how the question got on the ballot), the question’s page says so beside it. Each side’s arguments in the official voter guide are linked, never reprinted.
page

Your ballot, printed or kept. “As it will look” draws your ballot as a printed sample ballot; it is a preview, not an official ballot, and your county’s own sample ballot is the authority. “Keep this ballot on my phone” saves the contests, the names, the questions’ words and the names of your districts and places in this device’s own storage, with the date, to open with no signal. No location, no address and no account: nothing is sent anywhere. “Forget my location and choices” removes it, and so does “Forget this ballot” on the kept page. Anyone holding your unlocked phone can see which districts a kept ballot is for.

changelog.title: Top movers, and breaking-news alerts for Election Night
items: Top movers: a ticker on the Forecasts page, on Election Night's Forecasts page and on the front page shows the races whose forecast moved most since the previous day's, like a stock ticker: the state, the office, the leading candidate's chance and how many points it moved, and "now leads" where the lead changed hands. Each one opens the race's chart. It stops when you point at it or move to it with the keyboard, has a Pause button, and never moves for anyone who has Motion off, Calm on or reduced motion on their device: the races then sit in a row you can scroll. Labelled Analysis.

Election Night alerts: on the night (from 4 p.m. Central on November 3), a banner across the top of every page brings the news as it comes: polls closing in each state, each state's first official results, a race whose live forecast passes 95%, a new leader in the live forecast, and projections. An early projection comes when the model gives a candidate 99% or more with at least a quarter of the expected vote counted; a full projection, in a stronger brass band, from half counted. Each says how much is counted, is labelled Analysis and "as reported, not final", and the official count decides. A projection that stops holding is withdrawn in an alert of its own. Pause, See all alerts and Close are there; nothing makes a sound; before the night the pages ask for nothing.

On the Forecasts page each race says when its forecast was made, and from the standard level up a small line shows how the leading candidate's chance moved, run by run; the top of the page says when the newest run was made.

changelog.title: A sandbox, and Anthropic's prospectus four ways
items: A sandbox on the draft site, for experiments: in no menu, not on the live site, and every page asks search engines not to list it.

Its first experiment is the prospectus Anthropic, the company that makes Claude, filed with the SEC on October 26, 2026, four ways. As filed: a link to the official copy on SEC.gov. In chapters: save the official copy from SEC.gov and open it in a reader that rebuilds it into its 27 chapters, with highlights, notes, search, a page-by-page view as filed, and a PDF of a chapter, the chapters you marked, your notes alone or the whole filing. The copy and your notes stay on your device; this site never holds the filing's text. In five minutes: about 1,230 words in the filing's own order, in our words, checked claim by claim against the filing. And an analysis of whether it reads as if an AI wrote it: whether text carries a mark that says so (it does not, for anyone to read), and the word counts studies tie to AI writing, beside eight other prospectuses, four of them filed before ChatGPT existed. Every figure there is labelled Analysis and says what it cannot tell you.
The pages say the site is built with the help of Claude, and that Anthropic had no part in them.

attorney_general.t: The attorney general is the state's top lawyer. The office speaks for the state in court, advises state agencies and enforces consumer laws.
s: About Our Office, Minnesota Attorney General
About the Office of Attorney General, Arizona Attorney General

x.es: El procurador general es el principal abogado del estado. La oficina representa al estado ante los tribunales, asesora a las agencias estatales y hace cumplir las leyes de protección al consumidor.

coroner.t: The coroner looks into deaths that are sudden, violent or unexplained to find the cause. In those cases the coroner signs the death certificate.
s: Duties of Elected County Officials, Informational Bulletin No. 114, Kentucky Legislative Research Commission

x.es: El forense investiga las muertes repentinas, violentas o sin explicación para encontrar la causa. En esos casos, el forense firma el certificado de defunción.

council.t: The city or town council makes the city's laws. It also passes the budget and sets taxes and fees.
s: Kentucky Municipal Statutory Law, Informational Bulletin No. 145, Kentucky Legislative Research Commission
State and Local Government, Chapter 3 Part A: Local Government, Louisiana House of Representatives

x.es: El concejo de la ciudad o del pueblo hace las leyes de la ciudad. También aprueba el presupuesto y fija los impuestos y las tarifas.

county_attorney.t: The county attorney brings criminal cases in county courts and is also the lawyer for county government. In some states this office is called the state's attorney.
s: Duties of Elected County Officials, Informational Bulletin No. 114, Kentucky Legislative Research Commission
Texas Constitution, Article 5 (Judicial Department), Texas Legislature

x.es: El abogado del condado presenta casos penales en los tribunales del condado y también es el abogado del gobierno del condado. En algunos estados, este cargo se llama fiscal del estado.

county_auditor.t: The county auditor keeps the county's money records. In some states it also runs elections and keeps tax records; in Ohio it values property.
s: North Dakota Century Code chapter 11-13, County Auditor, North Dakota Legislative Branch
Minnesota Statutes chapter 384, County Auditor, Minnesota Revisor of Statutes
RCW 36.22, County auditor, Washington State Legislature
Ohio Revised Code 5713.01, County auditor as assessor

x.es: El auditor del condado lleva los registros del dinero del condado. En algunos estados también administra las elecciones y guarda los registros de impuestos; en Ohio, valora las propiedades.

county_commissioner.t: The county's governing board passes the budget, sets taxes and oversees services like roads. Its members are called commissioners, and in some places supervisors or police jurors.
s: North Dakota Century Code chapter 11-11, Board of County Commissioners, North Dakota Legislative Branch
State and Local Government, Chapter 3 Part A: Local Government, Louisiana House of Representatives

x.es: La junta de gobierno del condado aprueba el presupuesto, fija los impuestos y supervisa servicios como los caminos. Sus miembros se llaman comisionados y, en algunos lugares, supervisores o jurados de policía.

county_finance_officer.t: In a few South Dakota counties an elected finance officer does the auditor's work. That includes election jobs, like voter lists and candidate filings.
s: 2026 County Candidate Campaign Guide, South Dakota Secretary of State

x.es: En unos pocos condados de Dakota del Sur, un funcionario de finanzas elegido hace el trabajo del auditor. Eso incluye tareas electorales, como las listas de votantes y la presentación de candidaturas.

county_treasurer.t: The county treasurer collects property taxes and keeps the county's money safe. The office shares it with schools, cities and other districts, but does not set how much is owed.
s: North Dakota Century Code chapter 11-14, County Treasurer, North Dakota Legislative Branch
Minnesota Statutes chapter 385, County Treasurer, Minnesota Revisor of Statutes

x.es: El tesorero del condado cobra los impuestos sobre la propiedad y guarda de forma segura el dinero del condado. La oficina lo reparte entre escuelas, ciudades y otros distritos, pero no decide cuánto se debe.

governor.t: The governor is the state's top leader. The governor signs or vetoes new laws, names many state officials and leads the state's military forces.
s: Texas Constitution, Article 4 (Executive Department), Texas Legislature
Michigan Constitution of 1963, Article V (Executive Branch), Michigan Legislature

x.es: El gobernador es el líder principal del estado. El gobernador firma o veta las nuevas leyes, nombra a muchos funcionarios estatales y dirige las fuerzas militares del estado.

public_utilities_commissioner.t: This three-member South Dakota board oversees private power, gas and phone companies and their rates. It also approves sites for power plants, wind farms and power lines.
s: About the PUC, South Dakota Public Utilities Commission

x.es: Esta junta de Dakota del Sur, de tres miembros, supervisa a las empresas privadas de electricidad, gas y teléfono, y sus tarifas. También aprueba los lugares para centrales eléctricas, parques eólicos y líneas eléctricas.

register_of_deeds.t: The register of deeds keeps the county's land records, such as deeds and mortgages. In some states, like North Carolina, it also issues marriage licenses and keeps vital records.
s: About the Register of Deeds Office, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina
North Dakota Century Code chapter 11-18, County Recorder (recorder takes the register of deeds' duties), North Dakota Legislative Branch

x.es: El registrador de escrituras guarda los registros de tierras del condado, como escrituras e hipotecas. En algunos estados, como Carolina del Norte, también emite licencias de matrimonio y guarda los registros civiles.

school_and_public_lands_commissioner.t: South Dakota's commissioner of school and public lands manages land the state holds for its schools. The office leases it for grazing and minerals to earn money for the schools.
s: About the Commissioner, South Dakota Office of School and Public Lands

x.es: El comisionado de tierras escolares y públicas de Dakota del Sur administra las tierras que el estado tiene para sus escuelas. La oficina las arrienda para pastoreo y minerales a fin de ganar dinero para las escuelas.

secretary_of_state.t: In most states, the secretary of state runs elections and keeps records, such as business filings. Other duties differ by state.
s: Secretary of State Divisions & Programs, Nebraska Secretary of State

x.es: En la mayoría de los estados, el secretario de estado administra las elecciones y guarda registros, como los documentos que presentan las empresas. Las demás funciones varían según el estado.

sheriff.t: In most states the sheriff is the county's top law officer. The office keeps the peace, runs the jail and carries out court orders; in Kentucky it also collects property taxes.
s: Minnesota Statutes 387.03, Powers, duties, Minnesota Revisor of Statutes
Minnesota Statutes 387.11, County jail, Minnesota Revisor of Statutes
Duties of Elected County Officials, Informational Bulletin No. 114, Kentucky Legislative Research Commission

x.es: En la mayoría de los estados, el alguacil es el principal agente de la ley del condado. La oficina mantiene la paz, dirige la cárcel y cumple las órdenes de los tribunales; en Kentucky, también cobra los impuestos sobre la propiedad.

soil_water.t: These supervisors run a local district that helps landowners protect soil and water. The board sets plans and a budget and can help pay for the work.
s: Soil & Water Conservation Districts, Minnesota Board of Water and Soil Resources
Become a Soil and Water District Board Member, Missouri Department of Natural Resources
About Districts, North Carolina Department of Agriculture, Soil and Water Conservation

x.es: Estos supervisores dirigen un distrito local que ayuda a los propietarios de tierras a proteger el suelo y el agua. La junta fija planes y un presupuesto, y puede ayudar a pagar los trabajos.

state_auditor.t: The state auditor checks how state agencies spend public money and whether they follow the law. In many states it checks local governments too.

x.es: El auditor estatal revisa cómo las agencias del estado gastan el dinero público y si cumplen la ley. En muchos estados también revisa a los gobiernos locales.

state_house.t: The state House (called the Assembly or House of Delegates in some states) is the larger chamber. Its members write and vote on state laws and the state budget.
s: What is the Legislature?, Wisconsin State Legislature
Legislative Q&A, Colorado House of Representatives

x.es: La Cámara de Representantes del estado (llamada Asamblea o Cámara de Delegados en algunos estados) es la cámara más grande. Sus miembros redactan y votan las leyes estatales y el presupuesto del estado.

state_senate.t: The state Senate is the smaller of the Legislature's two chambers (Nebraska has only one). Senators write and vote on state laws and the state budget.
s: What is the Legislature?, Wisconsin State Legislature
Legislative Branch Function and Process, North Dakota Legislative Branch

x.es: El Senado estatal es la más pequeña de las dos cámaras de la Legislatura (Nebraska tiene solo una). Los senadores redactan y votan las leyes estatales y el presupuesto del estado.

state_treasurer.t: The state treasurer keeps the state's money safe. The office takes in and invests state money, pays it out, and in many states returns lost money to its owners.
s: Illinois Constitution, Article V, Section 18 (Treasurer - duties), Illinois General Assembly

x.es: El tesorero estatal guarda de forma segura el dinero del estado. La oficina recibe e invierte el dinero del estado, hace los pagos y, en muchos estados, devuelve el dinero perdido a sus dueños.

utility_board.t: These boards run a public utility, such as a power, water or city utility. They oversee the service and set its rates.
s: RCW 54.16.040, Public utility districts: electric energy, Washington State Legislature
What's So Special About Special Districts? (4th ed.), California Senate Local Government Committee

x.es: Estas juntas dirigen una empresa pública de servicios, como una de electricidad, de agua o de servicios de la ciudad. Supervisan el servicio y fijan sus tarifas.

water_board.t: Water district board members run a public district that supplies water, and in some places sewer service or farm water, to its area. They set its rates and budget.
s: What's So Special About Special Districts? (4th ed.), California Senate Local Government Committee

x.es: Los miembros de la junta de un distrito de suministro de agua dirigen un distrito público que suministra agua a su zona y, en algunos lugares, servicio de alcantarillado o agua para la agricultura. Fijan sus tarifas y su presupuesto.
